transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. Since the grill works but the main oven stays cold with the fan running, the most likely cause is that the fan heating element has failed. The fan motor proves it gets power, so if the element isn't glowing red hot (or is visibly broken/scorched), it needs replacing. Before we go there, please check: 1) Ensure the clock isn't flashing or set to a timer mode (which stops heat until manual); 2) With the oven off and cool, remove the rear inner cover to inspect the fan element for breaks or burns. If the element looks fine but still doesn't heat, it's likely an internal wiring or selector switch fault.

clock is set n nothing flashing, its in manual. i can isolate it at the cooker switch on the wall no prob. back panel has 4 screws, il have a look at the element once its cool. heard a small pop from inside near the back last time it worked tho

Since the clock and timer are confirmed correct, and the fan motor runs (proving power reaches the back of the cavity), the most likely cause is that the fan heating element itself has burnt out or its wiring has melted/broken at the connection points. Please switch off and isolate the cooker again. Once cool, remove the rear inner panel to inspect the ring-shaped element behind the fan. Look for any physical breaks in the element tube, heavy scorching, or loose/melted wires at the terminals. If you see damage there, that is your fault. If it looks physically fine but still doesn't heat when turned on (and most likely doesn't glow red), we may need to test it with a multimeter for continuity.
ok took the back panel off, theres a blister/split in the coil near the bottom with a black mark. no multimeter tho so cant test it. is that the element dead then?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, that blister and split suggests the fan heating element has failed internally. Because this is a mains-powered appliance with exposed live parts once the cover is off, you must not use the oven until an engineer replaces the element.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, il stop using it. model on the door frame says IFW 6330 IX. can i get the element n fit it myself or does it need an engineer?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, that blister and split suggests the fan heating element has failed internally. While some homeowners can replace elements on certain models, this is a mains-powered appliance involving live connections behind the rear panel. Given the visible damage and the risk of electrical shock or fire if not fitted correctly, you must have it replaced by a qualified engineer. Do not attempt to fit it yourself or use the oven until an engineer has completed the repair.
